A freehand pen sketch, not a true perspective, so this camera is approximate and says how far. Its storey lines and cornice are level and its verticals vertical, so the camera is level and square to the front (heading 270, due west in the footprint frame); the principal point's x is the panel's centre. PIXEL ASPECT 0.618 IS THE DRAUGHTSMAN'S, NOT A RESAMPLING: the sketch draws the front about 1.6 times taller than it is wide against the 1911 sheet's 16.5 m front and the heights the engraving's camera fixed, and held to 1.0 the fit runs the eye 200 m out (an elevation) and still leaves 16 px RMS, 30 px at the tower. So widths are read from this panel only as proportions of the front (the tower about 5.5 m across against the door-to-window spacing, the portico about 4.7 m), and heights only as which storey a thing stands in, never as metres.
